import { InjectRepository } from '@nestjs/typeorm';
import { ConfigService } from '@nestjs/config';
import { Repository } from 'typeorm';
import { createECDH, createHash, timingSafeEqual } from 'crypto';
import { User } from '../entities/user.entity';
import { AuthMethod } from '../entities/auth-method.entity';
import { TokenService } from './token.service';
import { SiweService } from './siwe.service';

@Injectable()
export class TestAuthService {
  private readonly logger = new Logger(TestAuthService.name);

  constructor(
    private configService: ConfigService,
    private tokenService: TokenService,
    private siweService: SiweService,
    @InjectRepository(User)
    private userRepository: Repository<User>,
    @InjectRepository(AuthMethod)
    private authMethodRepository: Repository<AuthMethod>
  ) {}

  /**
   * Test-only login that bypasses Core Kit entirely.
   * Guarded by TEST_LOGIN_SECRET env var — never available in production.
   *
   * Creates/finds user by email, generates a deterministic secp256k1 keypair,
   * and issues tokens. Returns the keypair so E2E tests can initialize vaults.
   */
  async testLogin(
    email: string,
    secret: string
  ): Promise<{
    accessToken: string;
    refreshToken: string;
    isNewUser: boolean;
    publicKeyHex: string;
    privateKeyHex: string;
  }> {
    // 1. Defense-in-depth: never allow in production regardless of env var
    const nodeEnv = this.configService.get<string>('NODE_ENV');
    if (nodeEnv === 'production') {
      throw new ForbiddenException('Test login is not available in production');
    }

    // 2. Validate TEST_LOGIN_SECRET with timing-safe comparison
    const expectedSecret = this.configService.get<string>('TEST_LOGIN_SECRET');
    if (!expectedSecret) {
      throw new ForbiddenException('Test login is not enabled');
    }
    const secretBuf = Buffer.from(secret);
    const expectedBuf = Buffer.from(expectedSecret);
    if (secretBuf.length !== expectedBuf.length || !timingSafeEqual(secretBuf, expectedBuf)) {
      throw new UnauthorizedException('Invalid test login secret');
    }

    // 2. Generate deterministic secp256k1 keypair from email
    const { publicKeyHex, privateKeyHex } = this.generateDeterministicKeypair(email);

    // 3. Find or create user by email (hash-based lookup)
    const normalizedEmail = email.toLowerCase().trim();
    const identifierHash = this.siweService.hashIdentifier(normalizedEmail);

    const existingMethod = await this.authMethodRepository.findOne({
      where: { type: 'email', identifierHash },
      relations: ['user'],
    });

    let user: User;
    let isNewUser = false;

    if (existingMethod) {
      user = existingMethod.user;
      // Update publicKey to match deterministic keypair (may differ from Core Kit key)
      if (user.publicKey !== publicKeyHex) {
        user.publicKey = publicKeyHex;
        await this.userRepository.save(user);
      }
      existingMethod.lastUsedAt = new Date();
      await this.authMethodRepository.save(existingMethod);
    } else {
      isNewUser = true;
      user = await this.userRepository.save({ publicKey: publicKeyHex });
      await this.authMethodRepository.save({
        userId: user.id,
        type: 'email',
        identifier: identifierHash,
        identifierHash,
        identifierDisplay: this.siweService.truncateEmail(normalizedEmail),
        lastUsedAt: new Date(),
      });
    }

    // 4. Issue tokens
    const tokens = await this.tokenService.createTokens(user.id, user.publicKey);

    this.logger.log(`Test login: userId=${user.id}, isNew=${isNewUser}`);

    return {
      accessToken: tokens.accessToken,
      refreshToken: tokens.refreshToken,
      isNewUser,
      publicKeyHex,
      privateKeyHex,
    };
  }

  /**
   * Generate a deterministic secp256k1 keypair from an email address.
   * Same email always produces the same keypair, enabling consistent
   * vault encryption across test runs.
   */
  private generateDeterministicKeypair(email: string): {
    publicKeyHex: string;
    privateKeyHex: string;
  } {
    // Derive 32-byte private key from email via SHA-256
    const seed = createHash('sha256')
      .update(`cipherbox-test-keypair:${email.toLowerCase().trim()}`)
      .digest();

    // Ensure the seed is a valid secp256k1 private key (must be in [1, n-1])
    const n = BigInt('0xFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFEBAAEDCE6AF48A03BBFD25E8CD0364141');
    let keyInt = BigInt('0x' + seed.toString('hex'));
    keyInt = (keyInt % (n - 1n)) + 1n;
    const privateKeyHex = keyInt.toString(16).padStart(64, '0');

    const ecdh = createECDH('secp256k1');
    ecdh.setPrivateKey(Buffer.from(privateKeyHex, 'hex'));
    const publicKeyHex = ecdh.getPublicKey().toString('hex'); // 65 bytes uncompressed

    return { publicKeyHex, privateKeyHex };
  }
}

{"parentUuid":"0fc6cbce-b63f-4cf9-bbf0-8c09cd3a1541","isSidechain":true,"userType":"external","cwd":"/Users/michael/Code/cipher-box/.claude/worktrees/agent-afc2b739","sessionId":"bf782b2f-e367-4b3e-983f-f44a69c91c4d","version":"2.1.63","gitBranch":"worktree-agent-afc2b739","agentId":"afc2b7397ae056206","slug":"stateless-wobbling-wall","message":{"model":"claude-opus-4-6","id":"msg_014FF5NjC6mmhQVudHuAiTcQ","type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"tool_use","id":"REDACTED","name":"Edit","input":{"replace_all":false,"file_path":"/Users/michael/Code/cipher-box/.claude/worktrees/agent-afc2b739/apps/api/src/auth/auth.service.ts","old_string":"  /**
   * Get all linked auth methods for a user.
   * Returns identifierDisplay (human-readable) for all method types.
   * Falls back to identifier if identifierDisplay is not set.
   */
  async getLinkedMethods(userId: string): Promise<AuthMethodResponseDto[]> {
    const methods = await this.authMethodRepository.find({
      where: { userId },
      order: { createdAt: 'ASC' },
    });

    return methods.map((method) => ({
      id: method.id,
      type: method.type,
      // H-09: Fall back to '[redacted]' instead of leaking raw identifier hash
      identifier: method.identifierDisplay || '[redacted]',
      lastUsedAt: method.lastUsedAt,
      createdAt: method.createdAt,
    }));
  }

  /**
   * Link a new auth method to an existing user account.
   *
   * For Google/email: verifies CipherBox-issued JWT to confirm ownership of the new method.
   * For wallet: verifies SIWE message+signature to confirm wallet ownership.
   *
   * Cross-account collision: if the auth method already belongs to a different user,
   * a BadRequestException is thrown (user must unlink from the other account first).
   */
  async linkMethod(userId: string, linkDto: LinkMethodDto): Promise<AuthMethodResponseDto[]> {
    // 1. Get the user
    const user = await this.userRepository.findOne({ where: { id: userId } });
    if (!user) {
      throw new UnauthorizedException('User not found');
    }

    const authMethodType = linkDto.loginType;

    if (authMethodType === 'wallet') {
      // Wallet linking: verify SIWE message + signature
      return this.linkWalletMethod(userId, linkDto);
    }

    // Google/email linking: verify CipherBox-issued JWT
    return this.linkJwtMethod(userId, linkDto);
  }

  /**
   * Link a Google or email auth method via CipherBox JWT verification.
   */
  private async linkJwtMethod(
    userId: string,
    linkDto: LinkMethodDto
  ): Promise<AuthMethodResponseDto[]> {
    // 1. Verify the CipherBox-issued JWT
    const payload = await this.verifyCipherBoxJwt(linkDto.idToken);

    // 2. Determine type and identifier, hash for lookup
    const authMethodType = linkDto.loginType;
    const identifier = payload.email || payload.sub;
    if (!identifier) {
      throw new BadRequestException('Cannot determine identifier from JWT');
    }
    const identifierHash = this.siweService.hashIdentifier(identifier);

    // 3. Check cross-account collision: same identifier linked to a different user
    const crossAccountMethod = await this.authMethodRepository.findOne({
      where: {
        type: authMethodType,
        identifierHash,
        userId: Not(userId),
      },
    });

    if (crossAccountMethod) {
      throw new BadRequestException(
        `This ${authMethodType === 'google' ? 'Google account' : 'email'} is already linked to another account`
      );
    }

    // 4. Check if this exact method is already linked to this user
    const existingMethod = await this.authMethodRepository.findOne({
      where: {
        userId,
        type: authMethodType,
        identifierHash,
      },
    });

    if (existingMethod) {
      throw new BadRequestException('This auth method is already linked to your account');
    }

    // 5. Create new AuthMethod entity with hashed identifier
    await this.authMethodRepository.save({
      userId,
      type: authMethodType,
      identifier: identifierHash,
      identifierHash,
      identifierDisplay: payload.email ? this.siweService.truncateEmail(payload.email) : identifier,
      lastUsedAt: new Date(),
    });

    // 6. Return updated list of methods
    return this.getLinkedMethods(userId);
  }

  /**
   * Link a wallet auth method via SIWE verification.
   */
  private async linkWalletMethod(
    userId: string,
    linkDto: LinkMethodDto
  ): Promise<AuthMethodResponseDto[]> {
    // 1. Validate required SIWE fields
    if (!linkDto.walletAddress || !linkDto.siweMessage || !linkDto.siweSignature) {
      throw new BadRequestException(
        'walletAddress, siweMessage, and siweSignature are required for wallet linking'
      );
    }

    // 2. Verify SIWE signature with nonce consumption (C-01: prevent replay)
    const parsed = parseSiweMessage(linkDto.siweMessage);
    if (!parsed.nonce) {
      throw new BadRequestException('Invalid SIWE message: missing nonce');
    }

    // Consume nonce from Redis (single-use) — same pattern as identity.controller.ts walletLogin
    const nonceKey = `siwe:nonce:${parsed.nonce}`;
    let nonceDeleted: number;
    try {
      nonceDeleted = await this.redis.del(nonceKey);
    } catch (err) {
      this.logger.error('Redis error during nonce consumption', err);
      throw new BadRequestException('Nonce verification failed');
    }
    if (!nonceDeleted) {
      throw new BadRequestException('Invalid or expired nonce');
    }

    const walletAddress = await this.siweService.verifySiweMessage(
      linkDto.siweMessage,
      linkDto.siweSignature as `0x${string}`,
      parsed.nonce
    );

    // 3. Hash the wallet address for lookup
    const addressHash = this.siweService.hashWalletAddress(walletAddress);

    // 4. Check cross-account collision: same wallet linked to a different user
    const crossAccountMethod = await this.authMethodRepository.findOne({
      where: {
        type: 'wallet',
        identifierHash: addressHash,
        userId: Not(userId),
      },
    });

    if (crossAccountMethod) {
      throw new BadRequestException('This wallet is already linked to another account');
    }

    // 5. Check if this wallet is already linked to this user
    const existingMethod = await this.authMethodRepository.findOne({
      where: {
        userId,
        type: 'wallet',
        identifierHash: addressHash,
      },
    });

    if (existingMethod) {
      throw new BadRequestException('This wallet is already linked to your account');
    }

    // 6. Create wallet auth method with hash + truncated display
    const truncated = this.siweService.truncateWalletAddress(walletAddress);
    await this.authMethodRepository.save({
      userId,
      type: 'wallet',
      identifier: addressHash,
      identifierHash: addressHash,
      identifierDisplay: truncated,
      lastUsedAt: new Date(),
    });

    // 7. Return updated list of methods
    return this.getLinkedMethods(userId);
  }

  /**
   * Unlink an auth method from a user account.
   * Cannot unlink the last remaining auth method.
   */
  async unlinkMethod(userId: string, methodId: string): Promise<void> {
    await this.authMethodRepository.manager.transaction(async (manager) => {
      // 1. Lock all auth methods for this user to prevent concurrent unlinks
      const methods = await manager
        .createQueryBuilder(AuthMethod, 'am')
        .setLock('pessimistic_write')
        .where('am.userId = :userId', { userId })
        .getMany();

      // 2. Find the target method
      const method = methods.find((m) => m.id === methodId);
      if (!method) {
        throw new BadRequestException('Auth method not found');
      }

      // 3. Cannot unlink if only 1 method remains
      if (methods.length <= 1) {
        throw new BadRequestException('Cannot unlink your last auth method');
      }

      // 4. Delete the method
      await manager.remove(method);
    });
  }

  /**
   * Test-only login that bypasses Core Kit entirely.
   * Guarded by TEST_LOGIN_SECRET env var — never available in production.
   *
   * Creates/finds user by email, generates a deterministic secp256k1 keypair,
   * and issues tokens. Returns the keypair so E2E tests can initialize vaults.
   */
  async testLogin(
    email: string,
    secret: string
  ): Promise<{
    accessToken: string;
    refreshToken: string;
    isNewUser: boolean;
    publicKeyHex: string;
    privateKeyHex: string;
  }> {
    // 1. Defense-in-depth: never allow in production regardless of env var
    const nodeEnv = this.configService.get<string>('NODE_ENV');
    if (nodeEnv === 'production') {
      throw new ForbiddenException('Test login is not available in production');
    }

    // 2. Validate TEST_LOGIN_SECRET with timing-safe comparison
    const expectedSecret = this.configService.get<string>('TEST_LOGIN_SECRET');
    if (!expectedSecret) {
      throw new ForbiddenException('Test login is not enabled');
    }
    const secretBuf = Buffer.from(secret);
    const expectedBuf = Buffer.from(expectedSecret);
    if (secretBuf.length !== expectedBuf.length || !timingSafeEqual(secretBuf, expectedBuf)) {
      throw new UnauthorizedException('Invalid test login secret');
    }

    // 2. Generate deterministic secp256k1 keypair from email
    const { publicKeyHex, privateKeyHex } = this.generateDeterministicKeypair(email);

    // 3. Find or create user by email (hash-based lookup)
    const normalizedEmail = email.toLowerCase().trim();
    const identifierHash = this.siweService.hashIdentifier(normalizedEmail);

    const existingMethod = await this.authMethodRepository.findOne({
      where: { type: 'email', identifierHash },
      relations: ['user'],
    });

    let user: User;
    let isNewUser = false;

    if (existingMethod) {
      user = existingMethod.user;
      // Update publicKey to match deterministic keypair (may differ from Core Kit key)
      if (user.publicKey !== publicKeyHex) {
        user.publicKey = publicKeyHex;
        await this.userRepository.save(user);
      }
      existingMethod.lastUsedAt = new Date();
      await this.authMethodRepository.save(existingMethod);
    } else {
      isNewUser = true;
      user = await this.userRepository.save({ publicKey: publicKeyHex });
      await this.authMethodRepository.save({
        userId: user.id,
        type: 'email',
        identifier: identifierHash,
        identifierHash,
        identifierDisplay: this.siweService.truncateEmail(normalizedEmail),
        lastUsedAt: new Date(),
      });
    }

    // 4. Issue tokens
    const tokens = await this.tokenService.createTokens(user.id, user.publicKey);

    this.logger.log(`Test login: userId=${user.id}, isNew=${isNewUser}`);

    return {
      accessToken: tokens.accessToken,
      refreshToken: tokens.refreshToken,
      isNewUser,
      publicKeyHex,
      privateKeyHex,
    };
  }

  /**
   * Generate a deterministic secp256k1 keypair from an email address.
   * Same email always produces the same keypair, enabling consistent
   * vault encryption across test runs.
   */
  private generateDeterministicKeypair(email: string): {
    publicKeyHex: string;
    privateKeyHex: string;
  } {
    // Derive 32-byte private key from email via SHA-256
    const seed = createHash('sha256')
      .update(`cipherbox-test-keypair:${email.toLowerCase().trim()}`)
      .digest();

    // Ensure the seed is a valid secp256k1 private key (must be in [1, n-1])
    const n = BigInt('0xFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFEBAAEDCE6AF48A03BBFD25E8CD0364141');
    let keyInt = BigInt('0x' + seed.toString('hex'));
    keyInt = (keyInt % (n - 1n)) + 1n;
    const privateKeyHex = keyInt.toString(16).padStart(64, '0');

    const ecdh = createECDH('secp256k1');
    ecdh.setPrivateKey(Buffer.from(privateKeyHex, 'hex'));
    const publicKeyHex = ecdh.getPublicKey().toString('hex'); // 65 bytes uncompressed

    return { publicKeyHex, privateKeyHex };
  }

   120→    /// Resolve FilePointer inodes by fetching and decrypting per-file IPNS metadata.
   121→    ///
   122→    /// This is called eagerly during populate_folder to ensure all files have correct
   123→    /// CID/key/IV/size BEFORE the first READDIR (NFS stability requirement).
   124→    fn resolve_file_pointers_blocking(
   125→        fs: &mut CipherBoxFS,
   126→        unresolved: &[(u64, String)],
   127→        folder_key: &[u8],
   128→    ) -> Result<(), String> {
   129→        let api = fs.api.clone();
   130→        let rt = fs.rt.clone();
   131→        let folder_key_arr: [u8; 32] = folder_key.try_into()
   132→            .map_err(|_| "Invalid folder key length for FilePointer resolution".to_string())?;
   133→
   134→        for (ino, ipns_name) in unresolved {
   135→            let resolve_result = block_with_timeout(&rt, async {
   136→                let resp = crate::api::ipns::resolve_ipns(&api, ipns_name).await?;
   137→                let encrypted_bytes = crate::api::ipfs::fetch_content(&api, &resp.cid).await?;
   138→                Ok::<Vec<u8>, String>(encrypted_bytes)
   139→            });
   140→
   141→            match resolve_result {
   142→                Ok(encrypted_bytes) => {
   143→                    // Decrypt file metadata JSON (same format as folder metadata: { iv, data })
   144→                    match crate::fuse::decrypt::decrypt_file_metadata_from_ipfs_public(&encrypted_bytes, &folder_key_arr) {
   145→                        Ok(file_meta) => {
   146→                            fs.inodes.resolve_file_pointer(
   147→                                *ino,
   148→                                file_meta.cid,
   149→                                file_meta.file_key_encrypted,
   150→                                file_meta.file_iv,
   151→                                file_meta.size,
   152→                                file_meta.encryption_mode,
   153→                                file_meta.versions,
   154→                            );
   155→                        }
   156→                        Err(e) => {
   157→                            log::warn!(
   158→                                "FilePointer resolution failed for ino {} ({}): {}",
   159→                                ino, ipns_name, e
   160→                            );
   161→                        }
   162→                    }
   163→                }
   164→                Err(e) => {
   165→                    log::warn!(
   166→                        "FilePointer IPNS resolve failed for ino {} ({}): {}",
   167→                        ino, ipns_name, e
   168→                    );
   169→                }
   170→            }
   171→        }
   172→
   173→        Ok(())
   174→    }

   176→    /// Helper: Fetch and decrypt existing file content for editing.
   177→    ///
   178→    /// Used when opening an existing file for writing -- need to pre-populate
   179→    /// the temp file with the current decrypted content.
   180→    /// Dispatches to AES-GCM or AES-CTR based on encryption_mode.
   181→    fn fetch_and_decrypt_file_content(
   182→        fs: &CipherBoxFS,
   183→        cid: &str,
   184→        encrypted_file_key_hex: &str,
   185→        iv_hex: &str,
   186→        encryption_mode: &str,
   187→    ) -> Result<Vec<u8>, String> {
   188→        let api = fs.api.clone();
   189→        let private_key = fs.private_key.clone();
   190→        let cid_owned = cid.to_string();
   191→        let key_hex = encrypted_file_key_hex.to_string();
   192→        let iv_hex_owned = iv_hex.to_string();
   193→        let mode = encryption_mode.to_string();
   194→        let rt = fs.rt.clone();
   195→
   196→        block_with_timeout(&rt, async {
   197→            let encrypted_bytes =
   198→                crate::api::ipfs::fetch_content(&api, &cid_owned).await?;
   199→            let encrypted_file_key = hex::decode(&key_hex)
   200→                .map_err(|_| "Invalid file key hex".to_string())?;
   201→            let file_key = zeroize::Zeroizing::new(
   202→                crate::crypto::ecies::unwrap_key(&encrypted_file_key, &private_key)
   203→                    .map_err(|e| format!("File key unwrap failed: {}", e))?,
   204→            );
   205→            let file_key_arr: [u8; 32] = file_key.as_slice().try_into()
   206→                .map_err(|_| "Invalid file key length".to_string())?;
   207→
   208→            let plaintext = if mode == "CTR" {
   209→                // AES-CTR: 16-byte IV, no auth tag
   210→                let iv = hex::decode(&iv_hex_owned)
   211→                    .map_err(|_| "Invalid file IV hex".to_string())?;
   212→                let iv_arr: [u8; 16] = iv.try_into()
   213→                    .map_err(|_| "Invalid CTR IV length (expected 16)".to_string())?;
   214→                crate::crypto::aes_ctr::decrypt_aes_ctr(&encrypted_bytes, &file_key_arr, &iv_arr)
   215→                    .map_err(|e| format!("CTR file decryption failed: {}", e))?
   216→            } else {
   217→                // AES-GCM: 12-byte IV, 16-byte auth tag appended
   218→                let iv = hex::decode(&iv_hex_owned)
   219→                    .map_err(|_| "Invalid file IV hex".to_string())?;
   220→                let iv_arr: [u8; 12] = iv.try_into()
   221→                    .map_err(|_| "Invalid GCM IV length (expected 12)".to_string())?;
   222→                crate::crypto::aes::decrypt_aes_gcm(
   223→                    &encrypted_bytes, &file_key_arr, &iv_arr,
   224→                )
   225→                .map_err(|e| format!("GCM file decryption failed: {}", e))?
   226→            };
   227→
   228→            Ok(plaintext)
   229→        })
   230→    }

   272→    /// Encrypt and publish per-file FileMetadata to the file's own IPNS record.
   273→    ///
   274→    /// Encrypts with parent folder key (matching web app behavior), uploads to IPFS,
   275→    /// creates signed IPNS record, and publishes via API.
   276→    async fn publish_file_metadata(
   277→        api: &crate::api::client::ApiClient,
   278→        file_meta: &crate::crypto::folder::FileMetadata,
   279→        folder_key: &[u8],
   280→        file_ipns_private_key: &zeroize::Zeroizing<Vec<u8>>,
   281→        file_ipns_name: &str,
   282→        coordinator: &crate::fuse::PublishCoordinator,
   283→    ) -> Result<(), String> {
   284→        let folder_key_arr: [u8; 32] = folder_key
   285→            .try_into()
   286→            .map_err(|_| "Invalid folder key length for FileMetadata encryption".to_string())?;
   287→
   288→        // Encrypt FileMetadata with parent folder key
   289→        let sealed = crate::crypto::folder::encrypt_file_metadata(file_meta, &folder_key_arr)
   290→            .map_err(|e| format!("FileMetadata encryption failed: {}", e))?;
   291→
   292→        // Package as JSON envelope: { "iv": hex, "data": base64 }
   293→        let iv_hex = hex::encode(&sealed[..12]);
   294→        use base64::Engine;
   295→        let data_base64 = base64::engine::general_purpose::STANDARD.encode(&sealed[12..]);
   296→        let json = serde_json::json!({ "iv": iv_hex, "data": data_base64 });
   297→        let json_bytes = serde_json::to_vec(&json)
   298→            .map_err(|e| format!("FileMetadata JSON serialization failed: {}", e))?;
   299→
   300→        // Upload encrypted file metadata to IPFS
   301→        let file_meta_cid = crate::api::ipfs::upload_content(api, &json_bytes).await?;
   302→
   303→        // Resolve current IPNS sequence number
   304→        let seq = coordinator.resolve_sequence(api, file_ipns_name).await?;
   305→
   306→        // Create and sign IPNS record
   307→        let ipns_key_arr: [u8; 32] = file_ipns_private_key.as_slice()
   308→            .try_into()
   309→            .map_err(|_| "Invalid file IPNS private key length".to_string())?;
   310→        let new_seq = seq + 1;
   311→        let value = format!("/ipfs/{}", file_meta_cid);
   312→        let record = crate::crypto::ipns::create_ipns_record(
   313→            &ipns_key_arr,
   314→            &value,
   315→            new_seq,
   316→            86_400_000, // 24h validity
   317→        )
   318→        .map_err(|e| format!("File IPNS record creation failed: {}", e))?;
   319→        let marshaled = crate::crypto::ipns::marshal_ipns_record(&record)
   320→            .map_err(|e| format!("File IPNS record marshal failed: {}", e))?;
   321→
   322→        let record_b64 = base64::engine::general_purpose::STANDARD.encode(&marshaled);
   323→
   324→        let req = crate::api::ipns::IpnsPublishRequest {
   325→            ipns_name: file_ipns_name.to_string(),
   326→            record: record_b64,
   327→            metadata_cid: file_meta_cid.clone(),
   328→            encrypted_ipns_private_key: None,
   329→            key_epoch: None,
   330→        };
   331→        crate::api::ipns::publish_ipns(api, &req).await?;
   332→
   333→        coordinator.record_publish(file_ipns_name, new_seq);
   334→        log::info!("Per-file IPNS publish succeeded for {}", file_ipns_name);
   335→
   336→        Ok(())
   337→    }

   109→    /// Resolve a Windows-style path (`\folder\subfolder\file.txt`) to (ino, parent_ino).
   110→    /// Returns None if any component is not found.
   111→    fn resolve_path(fs: &CipherBoxFS, path: &str) -> Option<(u64, u64)> {
   112→        let path = path.trim_start_matches('\\');
   113→        if path.is_empty() {
   114→            return Some((ROOT_INO, ROOT_INO));
   115→        }
   116→        let mut current_ino = ROOT_INO;
   117→        let mut parent_ino = ROOT_INO;
   118→        for component in path.split('\\').filter(|c| !c.is_empty()) {
   119→            parent_ino = current_ino;
   120→            match fs.inodes.find_child(current_ino, component) {
   121→                Some(child_ino) => current_ino = child_ino,
   122→                None => return None,
   123→            }
   124→        }
   125→        Some((current_ino, parent_ino))
   126→    }

   128→    /// Split a Windows path into (parent_path, file_name).
   129→    /// e.g. `\Documents\hello.txt` -> (`\Documents`, `hello.txt`)
   130→    /// Root path `\` or `\hello.txt` -> (`\`, `hello.txt`)
   131→    fn split_path(path: &str) -> (&str, &str) {
   132→        match path.rfind('\\') {
   133→            Some(pos) => {
   134→                let parent = if pos == 0 { "\\" } else { &path[..pos] };
   135→                let name = &path[pos + 1..];
   136→                (parent, name)
   137→            }
   138→            None => ("\\", path),
   139→        }
   140→    }

   144→    /// Convert a SystemTime to Windows FILETIME (100-nanosecond intervals
   145→    /// since 1601-01-01). Returns 0 if the time is before the Unix epoch.
   146→    fn systemtime_to_filetime(t: SystemTime) -> u64 {
   147→        // Windows FILETIME epoch: 1601-01-01 00:00:00 UTC
   148→        // Unix epoch: 1970-01-01 00:00:00 UTC
   149→        // Difference: 11644473600 seconds = 116444736000000000 in 100ns intervals
   150→        const EPOCH_DIFF: u64 = 116_444_736_000_000_000;
   151→        match t.duration_since(UNIX_EPOCH) {
   152→            Ok(d) => {
   153→                let hundred_ns = d.as_secs() * 10_000_000 + d.subsec_nanos() as u64 / 100;
   154→                hundred_ns + EPOCH_DIFF
   155→            }
   156→            Err(_) => 0,
   157→        }
   158→    }

   160→    /// Convert Windows FILETIME to SystemTime. Returns UNIX_EPOCH if invalid.
   161→    fn filetime_to_systemtime(ft: u64) -> SystemTime {
   162→        const EPOCH_DIFF: u64 = 116_444_736_000_000_000;
   163→        if ft < EPOCH_DIFF {
   164→            return UNIX_EPOCH;
   165→        }
   166→        let hundred_ns = ft - EPOCH_DIFF;
   167→        let secs = hundred_ns / 10_000_000;
   168→        let nanos = (hundred_ns % 10_000_000) * 100;
   169→        UNIX_EPOCH + Duration::new(secs, nanos as u32)
   170→    }

## Task: Split FUSE operations.rs files by category

**Goal:** Split the large FUSE operations files into category-based modules:
- `apps/desktop/src-tauri/src/fuse/operations.rs` (2,363 lines — macOS FUSE-T)
- `apps/desktop/src-tauri/src/fuse/windows/operations.rs` (2,489 lines — Windows/Dokany)

### Target Structure for EACH platform:
1. **`read_ops.rs`** — Read operations: `read`, `open`, `release`, `getattr`, `lookup`, `access`
2. **`write_ops.rs`** — Write operations: `write`, `create`, `setattr`, `rename`, `unlink`, `rmdir`, `mkdir`, `mknod`
3. **`dir_ops.rs`** — Directory operations: `readdir`, `opendir`, `releasedir`, `statfs`
4. **`operations.rs`** — Slimmed down: trait impl that delegates to the category modules, shared types/helpers

### Important Rust Pattern:
- In Rust, you CANNOT split a `impl Trait for Struct` across multiple files
- The pattern is: impl methods in operations.rs call helper functions defined in the sub-modules
- Example:
  ```rust
  // operations.rs
  mod read_ops;
  mod write_ops;
  mod dir_ops;
  
  impl fuser::Filesystem for CipherBoxFS {
      fn read(&mut self, req, ino, ...) { read_ops::handle_read(self, req, ino, ...) }
      fn write(&mut self, req, ino, ...) { write_ops::handle_write(self, req, ino, ...) }
      // etc.
  }
  ```
- Each sub-module gets functions like `pub(crate) fn handle_read(fs: &mut CipherBoxFS, ...)` that contain the actual logic

### Steps:
1. Read both `operations.rs` files fully
2. Read the parent module files to understand how operations.rs is imported
3. For each platform, identify which methods go in which category
4. Create the sub-modules with extracted logic as free functions
5. Slim down operations.rs to delegate to the sub-modules

### Verification:
Run `cd /Users/michael/Code/cipher-box/apps/desktop/src-tauri && cargo check 2>&1 | tail -20` to verify compilation.

    59→    /// Run an async operation with a timeout, blocking the current thread.

    61→    fn block_with_timeout<F, T>(rt: &tokio::runtime::Handle, fut: F) -> Result<T, String>
    62→    where
    63→        F: std::future::Future<Output = Result<T, String>>,
    64→    {
    65→        rt.block_on(async {
    66→            match tokio::time::timeout(NETWORK_TIMEOUT, fut).await {

    68→                Err(_) => Err("Operation timed out".to_string()),
    69→            }

    78→    fn fetch_and_populate_folder(
    79→        fs: &mut CipherBoxFS,
    80→        ino: u64,
    81→        ipns_name: &str,
    82→        folder_key: &[u8],
    83→    ) -> Result<(), String> {

    86→        let folder_key_owned = folder_key.to_vec();
    87→        let private_key = fs.private_key.clone();
    88→
    89→        let rt = fs.rt.clone();

    92→                crate::api::ipns::resolve_ipns(&api, &ipns_name_owned).await?;
    93→            let encrypted_bytes =
    94→                crate::api::ipfs::fetch_content(&api, &resolve_resp.cid).await?;
    95→            Ok::<(Vec<u8>, String), String>((encrypted_bytes, resolve_resp.cid))
    96→        })?;
    97→
    98→        let (encrypted_bytes, cid) = result;
    99→
   100→        // Decrypt metadata (v2 only)
   101→        let metadata = crate::fuse::decrypt::decrypt_metadata_from_ipfs_public(&encrypted_bytes, &folder_key_owned)?;
   102→
   103→        // Cache metadata directly
   104→        fs.metadata_cache.set(&ipns_name.to_string(), metadata.clone(), cid);
   105→
   106→        // Populate inode table with children.
   107→        // First load for this folder -- replace mode (merge_only=false).

   124→    fn resolve_file_pointers_blocking(

   132→            .map_err(|_| "Invalid folder key length for FilePointer resolution".to_string())?;

   134→        for (ino, ipns_name) in unresolved {

   138→                Ok::<Vec<u8>, String>(encrypted_bytes)
   139→            });

   141→            match resolve_result {
   142→                Ok(encrypted_bytes) => {
   143→                    // Decrypt file metadata JSON (same format as folder metadata: { iv, data })
   144→                    match crate::fuse::decrypt::decrypt_file_metadata_from_ipfs_public(&encrypted_bytes, &folder_key_arr) {

   146→                            fs.inodes.resolve_file_pointer(
   147→                                *ino,

   151→                                file_meta.size,
   152→                                file_meta.encryption_mode,
   153→                                file_meta.versions,
   154→                            );
   155→                        }

   158→                                "FilePointer resolution failed for ino {} ({}): {}",
   159→                                ino, ipns_name, e
   160→                            );
   161→                        }
   162→                    }
   163→                }
   164→                Err(e) => {
   165→                    log::warn!(
   166→                        "FilePointer IPNS resolve failed for ino {} ({}): {}",
   167→                        ino, ipns_name, e
   168→                    );
   169→                }
   170→            }
   171→        }

   176→    /// Helper: Fetch and decrypt existing file content for editing.
   177→    ///
   178→    /// Used when opening an existing file for writing -- need to pre-populate
   179→    /// the temp file with the current decrypted content.
   180→    /// Dispatches to AES-GCM or AES-CTR based on encryption_mode.
   181→    fn fetch_and_decrypt_file_content(
   182→        fs: &CipherBoxFS,
   183→        cid: &str,
   184→        encrypted_file_key_hex: &str,
   185→        iv_hex: &str,
   186→        encryption_mode: &str,
   187→    ) -> Result<Vec<u8>, String> {
   188→        let api = fs.api.clone();
   189→        let private_key = fs.private_key.clone();
   190→        let cid_owned = cid.to_string();
   191→        let key_hex = encrypted_file_key_hex.to_string();
   192→        let iv_hex_owned = iv_hex.to_string();
   193→        let mode = encryption_mode.to_string();
   194→        let rt = fs.rt.clone();
   195→
   196→        block_with_timeout(&rt, async {
   197→            let encrypted_bytes =
   198→                crate::api::ipfs::fetch_content(&api, &cid_owned).await?;
   199→            let encrypted_file_key = hex::decode(&key_hex)
   200→                .map_err(|_| "Invalid file key hex".to_string())?;
   201→            let file_key = zeroize::Zeroizing::new(
   202→                crate::crypto::ecies::unwrap_key(&encrypted_file_key, &private_key)
   203→                    .map_err(|e| format!("File key unwrap failed: {}", e))?,
   204→            );
   205→            let file_key_arr: [u8; 32] = file_key.as_slice().try_into()
   206→                .map_err(|_| "Invalid file key length".to_string())?;
   207→
   208→            let plaintext = if mode == "CTR" {
   209→                // AES-CTR: 16-byte IV, no auth tag
   210→                let iv = hex::decode(&iv_hex_owned)
   211→                    .map_err(|_| "Invalid file IV hex".to_string())?;
   212→                let iv_arr: [u8; 16] = iv.try_into()
   213→                    .map_err(|_| "Invalid CTR IV length (expected 16)".to_string())?;
   214→                crate::crypto::aes_ctr::decrypt_aes_ctr(&encrypted_bytes, &file_key_arr, &iv_arr)
   215→                    .map_err(|e| format!("CTR file decryption failed: {}", e))?
   216→            } else {
   217→                // AES-GCM: 12-byte IV, 16-byte auth tag appended
   218→                let iv = hex::decode(&iv_hex_owned)
   219→                    .map_err(|_| "Invalid file IV hex".to_string())?;
   220→                let iv_arr: [u8; 12] = iv.try_into()
   221→                    .map_err(|_| "Invalid GCM IV length (expected 12)".to_string())?;
   222→                crate::crypto::aes::decrypt_aes_gcm(
   223→                    &encrypted_bytes, &file_key_arr, &iv_arr,
   224→                )
   225→                .map_err(|e| format!("GCM file decryption failed: {}", e))?
   226→            };
   227→
   228→            Ok(plaintext)
   229→        })
   230→    }

   272→    /// Encrypt and publish per-file FileMetadata to the file's own IPNS record.
   273→    ///
   274→    /// Encrypts with parent folder key (matching web app behavior), uploads to IPFS,
   275→    /// creates signed IPNS record, and publishes via API.
   276→    async fn publish_file_metadata(
   277→        api: &crate::api::client::ApiClient,
   278→        file_meta: &crate::crypto::folder::FileMetadata,
   279→        folder_key: &[u8],
   280→        file_ipns_private_key: &zeroize::Zeroizing<Vec<u8>>,
   281→        file_ipns_name: &str,
   282→        coordinator: &crate::fuse::PublishCoordinator,
   283→    ) -> Result<(), String> {
   284→        let folder_key_arr: [u8; 32] = folder_key
   285→            .try_into()
   286→            .map_err(|_| "Invalid folder key length for FileMetadata encryption".to_string())?;
   287→
   288→        // Encrypt FileMetadata with parent folder key
   289→        let sealed = crate::crypto::folder::encrypt_file_metadata(file_meta, &folder_key_arr)
   290→            .map_err(|e| format!("FileMetadata encryption failed: {}", e))?;
   291→
   292→        // Package as JSON envelope: { "iv": hex, "data": base64 }
   293→        let iv_hex = hex::encode(&sealed[..12]);
   294→        use base64::Engine;
   295→        let data_base64 = base64::engine::general_purpose::STANDARD.encode(&sealed[12..]);
   296→        let json = serde_json::json!({ "iv": iv_hex, "data": data_base64 });
   297→        let json_bytes = serde_json::to_vec(&json)
   298→            .map_err(|e| format!("FileMetadata JSON serialization failed: {}", e))?;
   299→
   300→        // Upload encrypted file metadata to IPFS
   301→        let file_meta_cid = crate::api::ipfs::upload_content(api, &json_bytes).await?;
   302→
   303→        // Resolve current IPNS sequence number
   304→        let seq = coordinator.resolve_sequence(api, file_ipns_name).await?;
   305→
   306→        // Create and sign IPNS record
   307→        let ipns_key_arr: [u8; 32] = file_ipns_private_key.as_slice()
   308→            .try_into()
   309→            .map_err(|_| "Invalid file IPNS private key length".to_string())?;
   310→        let new_seq = seq + 1;
   311→        let value = format!("/ipfs/{}", file_meta_cid);
   312→        let record = crate::crypto::ipns::create_ipns_record(
   313→            &ipns_key_arr,
   314→            &value,
   315→            new_seq,
   316→            86_400_000, // 24h validity
   317→        )
   318→        .map_err(|e| format!("File IPNS record creation failed: {}", e))?;
   319→        let marshaled = crate::crypto::ipns::marshal_ipns_record(&record)
   320→            .map_err(|e| format!("File IPNS record marshal failed: {}", e))?;
   321→
   322→        let record_b64 = base64::engine::general_purpose::STANDARD.encode(&marshaled);
   323→
   324→        let req = crate::api::ipns::IpnsPublishRequest {
   325→            ipns_name: file_ipns_name.to_string(),
   326→            record: record_b64,
   327→            metadata_cid: file_meta_cid.clone(),
   328→            encrypted_ipns_private_key: None,
   329→            key_epoch: None,
   330→        };
   331→        crate::api::ipns::publish_ipns(api, &req).await?;
   332→
   333→        coordinator.record_publish(file_ipns_name, new_seq);
   334→        log::info!("Per-file IPNS publish succeeded for {}", file_ipns_name);
   335→
   336→        Ok(())
   337→    }

   339→    impl Filesystem for CipherBoxFS {
   340→        /// Initialize the filesystem.
   341→        ///
   342→        /// Root folder is pre-populated in mount_filesystem() before the FUSE
   343→        /// event loop starts. No network I/O happens here — FUSE-T's NFS layer
   344→        /// requires fast init() responses to avoid connection timeouts.
   345→        fn init(
   346→            &mut self,
   347→            _req: &Request<'_>,
   348→            _config: &mut fuser::KernelConfig,
   349→        ) -> Result<(), libc::c_int> {
   350→            log::info!("CipherBoxFS::init (root pre-populated, no network I/O)");
   351→            log::info!("Root IPNS name: {}", self.root_ipns_name);
   352→            log::info!("Inode count: {}", self.inodes.inodes.len());
   353→            Ok(())
   354→        }

   356→        /// Clean up all caches and zeroize sensitive data on unmount.
   357→        fn destroy(&mut self) {
   358→            use zeroize::Zeroize;
   359→
   360→            self.content_cache.clear();
   361→            self.metadata_cache.clear();
   362→
   363→            // Zeroize pending_content values
   364→            for (_, content) in self.pending_content.iter_mut() {
   365→                content.zeroize();
   366→            }
   367→            self.pending_content.clear();
   368→
   369→            // Zeroize open file handles' cached content
   370→            for (_, handle) in self.open_files.iter_mut() {
   371→                if let Some(ref mut c) = handle.cached_content {
   372→                    c.zeroize();
   373→                }
   374→            }
   375→            self.open_files.clear();
   376→
   377→            log::info!("CipherBoxFS destroyed: all caches zeroized");
   378→        }

   380→        /// Look up a child by name within a parent directory.
   381→        fn lookup(
   382→            &mut self,
   383→            _req: &Request<'_>,
   384→            parent: u64,
   385→            name: &OsStr,
   386→            reply: ReplyEntry,
   387→        ) {
   388→            self.drain_upload_completions();
   389→            self.drain_refresh_completions();
   390→
   391→            let name_str = match name.to_str() {
   392→                Some(n) => n,
   393→                None => {
   394→                    reply.error(libc::ENOENT);
   395→                    return;
   396→                }
   397→            };
   398→
   399→            // Handle "." and ".." — NFS clients rely on these working.
   400→            // Returning ENOENT for ".." causes the NFS client to disconnect.
   401→            if name_str == "." {
   402→                if let Some(inode) = self.inodes.get(parent) {
   403→                    reply.entry(&ttl_for_is_dir(inode.attr.is_dir), &inode.attr.to_fuse_attr(current_uid(), current_gid()), 0);
   404→                    return;
   405→                }
   406→            }
   407→            if name_str == ".." {
   408→                let parent_ino = self.inodes.get(parent)

   160→    /// Convert Windows FILETIME to SystemTime. Returns UNIX_EPOCH if invalid.
   161→    fn filetime_to_systemtime(ft: u64) -> SystemTime {
   162→        const EPOCH_DIFF: u64 = 116_444_736_000_000_000;
   163→        if ft < EPOCH_DIFF {
   164→            return UNIX_EPOCH;
   165→        }
   166→        let hundred_ns = ft - EPOCH_DIFF;
   167→        let secs = hundred_ns / 10_000_000;
   168→        let nanos = (hundred_ns % 10_000_000) * 100;
   169→        UNIX_EPOCH + Duration::new(secs, nanos as u32)
   170→    }

   301→    /// Encrypt and publish per-file FileMetadata to the file's own IPNS record.
   302→    async fn publish_file_metadata(
   303→        api: &crate::api::client::ApiClient,
   304→        file_meta: &crate::crypto::folder::FileMetadata,
   305→        folder_key: &[u8],
   306→        file_ipns_private_key: &zeroize::Zeroizing<Vec<u8>>,
   307→        file_ipns_name: &str,
   308→        coordinator: &crate::fuse::PublishCoordinator,
   309→    ) -> Result<(), String> {
   310→        let folder_key_arr: [u8; 32] = folder_key.try_into().map_err(|_| {
   311→            "Invalid folder key length for FileMetadata encryption".to_string()
   312→        })?;
   313→
   314→        // Encrypt FileMetadata with parent folder key
   315→        let sealed =
   316→            crate::crypto::folder::encrypt_file_metadata(file_meta, &folder_key_arr)
   317→                .map_err(|e| format!("FileMetadata encryption failed: {}", e))?;
   318→
   319→        // Package as JSON envelope: { "iv": hex, "data": base64 }
   320→        let iv_hex = hex::encode(&sealed[..12]);
   321→        use base64::Engine;
   322→        let data_base64 =
   323→            base64::engine::general_purpose::STANDARD.encode(&sealed[12..]);
   324→        let json = serde_json::json!({ "iv": iv_hex, "data": data_base64 });
   325→        let json_bytes = serde_json::to_vec(&json)
   326→            .map_err(|e| format!("FileMetadata JSON serialization failed: {}", e))?;
   327→
   328→        // Upload encrypted file metadata to IPFS
   329→        let file_meta_cid =
   330→            crate::api::ipfs::upload_content(api, &json_bytes).await?;
   331→
   332→        // Resolve current IPNS sequence number
   333→        let seq = coordinator
   334→            .resolve_sequence(api, file_ipns_name)
   335→            .await?;
   336→
   337→        // Create and sign IPNS record
   338→        let ipns_key_arr: [u8; 32] = file_ipns_private_key
   339→            .as_slice()
   340→            .try_into()
   341→            .map_err(|_| "Invalid file IPNS private key length".to_string())?;
   342→        let new_seq = seq + 1;
   343→        let value = format!("/ipfs/{}", file_meta_cid);
   344→        let record = crate::crypto::ipns::create_ipns_record(
   345→            &ipns_key_arr,
   346→            &value,
   347→            new_seq,
   348→            86_400_000,
   349→        )
   350→        .map_err(|e| format!("File IPNS record creation failed: {}", e))?;
   351→        let marshaled = crate::crypto::ipns::marshal_ipns_record(&record)
   352→            .map_err(|e| format!("File IPNS record marshal failed: {}", e))?;
   353→
   354→        let record_b64 =
   355→            base64::engine::general_purpose::STANDARD.encode(&marshaled);
   356→
   357→        let req = crate::api::ipns::IpnsPublishRequest {
   358→            ipns_name: file_ipns_name.to_string(),
   359→            record: record_b64,
   360→            metadata_cid: file_meta_cid.clone(),
   361→            encrypted_ipns_private_key: None,
   362→            key_epoch: None,
   363→        };
   364→        crate::api::ipns::publish_ipns(api, &req).await?;
   365→
   366→        coordinator.record_publish(file_ipns_name, new_seq);
   367→        log::info!("Per-file IPNS publish succeeded for {}", file_ipns_name);
   368→
   369→        Ok(())
   370→    }
